title: Classify P104 lattices invariant under local Clifford gates (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-rank mathematical proof with finite corroboration. Every nonzero Gaussian-integer module invariant under every local P104 butterfly and single-bit i phase is a Gaussian scalar multiple of Clear1nsight’s #3382 Newton lattice:

```text
O[A,B] = M_2(O)  ->  tensor matrix units give M_(2^r)(O)
E_r^-1 L = J^(2^r), J an ideal of Z[i]  ->  L = alpha B_r
```

For every nonzero scalar alpha and rank r>=1, `alpha*(1+i)^max(r,4)*x_1*...*x_r` belongs to L and has integral quarter outside L. Consequently a different uniform invariant lattice cannot repair quarter-ADD closure in this fixed alphabet. A source-dependent divisibility filtration remains possible. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

The initial advance claim overlapped merged #3382’s exactness/maximality/phase theorem. The [public scope correction](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19221942) credits that result. This PR claims only the subsequent integral-order rigidity theorem and its universal quarter-closure consequence; predecessor results are cited, not re-audited.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Clear1nsight #3382 for the Newton lattice, maximal integral entrance and coefficient intertwiners; Ross Richardson #3068 for the closure boundary; Tekalign #3025/#3033 for lifting; Nick Petalas #3035/#3037, Arham Tahir #3046, ywz65 #2586 and the retained P104/native/geometry lineage. Matrix-unit and principal-ideal arguments are classical; their application to this fixed integral order is the new step.

## Evidence

- Four exact local matrix-unit words and all sixteen multiplication laws pass. The displayed identity has Gaussian-unit coefficient, so no denominator is inverted.
- Every one of the 21,844 tensor matrix-unit actions through rank seven passes. The written tensor proof establishes the operator claim; the dense action fixtures alone would not.
- A complete census of all 67 additive subgroups of `(Z[i]/2)^2`, imposing i and both generators, leaves exactly zero, the coordinatewise pi ideal, and the whole module.
- 168 signed scalar-ideal generator checks and 49 integral-quarter counterexamples pass. The C-only skew-lattice control demonstrates why the phase hypothesis matters.
- CPython 3.12.15 / macOS arm64, standard library only: normal and optimized warning-strict checks pass, about 3.1 seconds each (120-second limit). Registered metadata/replay and committed-byte/source-history checks pass for all six package files at `bfdea71502f026071e7dda46d2e15f540d3306cb`. Each verifier run generates a receipt bound to all six file hashes.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem requires Gaussian-module closure and every local butterfly/phase generator. It does not classify a smaller actual alphabet, nonadditive/correlated domains or states exact only after a completed word. Quarter closure is the uniform implication `f in L and f/4 integral => f/4 in L`; a stronger source entrance `4L -> L` is not excluded.

PR3382’s all-rank maximality and coefficient intertwiners are cited mathematical premises. No predecessor scientific replay, selected cold replay, native/physical realization, full caller, codec/storage/tape tariff, recursive invoice, Lean/Docker run or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Bind a divisibility filtration through quarter ADDs to one actual caller, with its exact scalar coefficients, phases, codec, independent targets and full native/storage bill.
2. Fix a smaller caller-specific generator alphabet and test whether a useful nonhomothetic domain survives; removing a phase already permits a skew lattice. A favourable complete cost is still required.

## Related open work

No open PR on this invariant-module classification or uniform integral-quarter closure was found in the refreshed open list and targeted Newton/lattice searches.

- #5964 bounds rounded errors on two later P104 gauge words; it does not classify invariant Newton lattices or supply this exact entrance contract. No shared number is computed here.
- #5967 studies pointwise tensor independence of the full Clifford group, rather than integral invariant modules of its local generators. No Gram threshold is computed or compared here.

Merged #3382 is the direct mathematical predecessor; its exactness result is retained with full credit.
